film.title: Toledo, Ohio: A Hundred Dollars to Fumble
film.description:
From about 2004 to 2006, two gamblers from the Detroit area paid University of Toledo football and basketball players cash, meals and groceries to shave points. By the government's account, one payment was a hundred dollars to fumble in a bowl game Toledo won 45-13. Seven former players pleaded guilty and got probation. Twenty years later the bookie is an app, and it is worth asking who the real criminal is.

Narrated by Matthew Hagan. Gary Mercer and Tessa Morales are fictional AI anchors with AI voices. The narrator is real. One short transition uses an AI-generated effect and is labeled on screen.

Local history... and college basketball. See more at https://hardwoodbricks.com

Recorded November 15, 2026. The Emmanuel Clase trial in Brooklyn was under way with no verdict at that time. Clase and Terry Rozier have pleaded not guilty.

Sources:
U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Michigan (indictment and pleas, 2009 to 2015)
Associated Press and ESPN reporting on the Toledo case (2007 to 2015)
Massachusetts Gaming Commission, September 30, 2025; WBUR, October 17, 2025
The Philadelphia Inquirer, September 3, 2026
The New York Times, November 20, 2022

Game footage: Toledo at Bowling Green, November 22, 2005, ESPN2, a short excerpt used under fair use for commentary. Photographs by Matthew Hagan. Other pictures from Wikimedia Commons, credited on screen.

reels.title: Who is the real criminal? Toledo, Ohio, 2005 to today
reels.text: A college kid takes a hundred dollars and it is a federal case. A sportsbook limits the winners and rewards the losers and it is a business model. A minute from our new film, Toledo, Ohio: A Hundred Dollars to Fumble.
